### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **85** documentable anchor(s).

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type/:name (route, 45 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aa4088fb62fc55e7b189296d21626638d77ac137` — the merge of head `026362a05da0d6190d7702bb77443af1c5d67b3c` into base `e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aa4088fb62fc55e7b189296d21626638d77ac137 && git checkout aa4088fb62fc55e7b189296d21626638d77ac137
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd 026362a05da0d6190d7702bb77443af1c5d67b3c && git checkout -B drift-repro e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd && git merge --no-ff 026362a05da0d6190d7702bb77443af1c5d67b3c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e06d04f9454559d65fcd1fd7a0727f9447cd94fd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `78122ffe9670072ca51541dfa4d502aa87e9541c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/batch-object-registration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/metadata-registry-question-producers.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`restoringOnRefusal`, `objectRegistrationRefusal`, `judgeRegistrationDoors`), packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts (`recordCurrencyFollowRefusal`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (the `manifest` service's one-run artifact registration, `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts (`applyObjectRegistryMutation`, `applyRegistryWriteThrough`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`restoreVersion`, `delete`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-unmanaged-import.ts (`rollBackUnmanagedImport`), `undoLandedPromotions` (PR #32454), packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts (the `external-import` call site): read at the head, not reviewed. Prose faces: .changeset/32369-batch-object-registration.md (semver, ②), content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx.

Inputs read: card #32369 body and its four comments (6782529809 scope addition, 6782781453 triage, 6806152283 claim, 6808545455 os-dev-report); PR #32474 body, file list (10 files, +1099/-24) and the net diff against `main`; the check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-11T22:34Z (52 runs): 29 success, 15 skipped by path filter, 8 in progress, 0 failed. Success includes Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, every Lint family, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Test UI, Check Documentation Links. Still in progress at that read: Test Core (1/8) to (8/8). Their conclusions are not in this record; the test evidence below is read off the diff, not off a green Test Core.

### ① Derived judgments

- `external-import` joins `AGAINST_REGISTRY_SAVE_FACES`: stored + success moves to `422 INVALID_METADATA`, nothing stored. RIGHT. The one call site (`service-datasource/src/plugin.ts`, `persistObject`) sends one `saveMetaItem` with no `mode`, which `saveMetaItem` resolves to `publish`, so `saveRegistryQuestion` answers `against-registry`; a draft on the face stays `body-only` (pinned). It refuses exactly what `meta-envelope` refuses for the same body.
- `duplicatePackage`: `copied[]` moves to `failed[]`, the copy taken back. RIGHT as a narrowing. The refusals are the registry's own (registration verbs replayed "verb for verb", then `objectRegistrationRefusal(..., { againstRegistry: true })`). The #29673 case holds by construction (passes retry a refused row once a sibling registers; the against-registry question is asked only when the whole unit is in) and is pinned (child before parent).
- `importUnmanagedPackage`: imported moves to `422 INVALID_METADATA` through `rollBackUnmanagedImport`. RIGHT. Same judge, the existing rollback, the registry's code and status carried on the thrown error; #29673 pinned (line before invoice).
- `publishPackageDrafts`: published moves to refused, the row as the causal `failed[]` entry. RIGHT as a narrowing. The D6 sibling case (a roll-up published before the draft that makes its child amount follow) is pinned and now registers in unit order in Phase 2. See ④ F2 for the non-transactional route.
- `migrateStoredMetadata`: `rewritten` moves to `failed`, the row restored. RIGHT as a narrowing, declared. Note for the maintainer's word: a row whose pair was already refused-by-single-save but tolerated by the boot can no longer be rewritten until the pair is corrected (the changeset says so in its "Was / now" and its author step).
- `registerApp` after `kernel:bootstrapped` (step 2c): registered moves to `422 INVALID_METADATA`. WRONG as scoped: it is not a pure narrowing. The judged unit is one package body, but after the seal the `manifest` service registers every body of an artifact, then the residual's objects, in ONE `restoringOnRefusal` run (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, the #31564 block; each `registerApp` joins it). Step 2c runs at the end of EACH body, so a valid artifact whose pair spans members is refused where it registered before. See ④ F1 (must-fix).
- Declared unmoved, confirmed in the tree: the cold boot (`bareNameHoldersAreSealed` is false until `kernel:bootstrapped`, so step 2c does not run and `objectRegistrationRefusal` drops `againstRegistry`), the stored-row hydration and `restoreArtifactRegistryView` (plain `registerObject`, no follow door), a draft save (`body-only`), a pair whose other end is not registered (no verdict in `recordCurrencyFollowRefusal`), extensions-only bodies (an `extend` body is `partial`: only its own `record` roll-ups are judged).
- Public surface: no export, schema key, route or error code added or removed. `AGAINST_REGISTRY_SAVE_FACES` gains a member; `REGISTRY_QUESTION_PRODUCERS` rows reworded; one new internal module. No `packages/spec` path in the diff.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/32369-batch-object-registration.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor. Matches the rule (kind `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves); these are the two packages whose `src` the diff moves outside tests. `packages/runtime` moves a test only.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset; the title carries `!`; the BREAKING banner and the FROM/TO list are in both; the ADR-0087 marker is present (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and no key is retired, so that disposition is right. `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- The changeset's sentence "A row whose pair a later row of the same batch completes still succeeds" is true of the four batch writers and false of a running install whose pair spans the members of one artifact (F1). It moves with the F1 fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1 (install/reload caller named, not edited): ANSWERED, holds. `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` answers a register refusal that declares a 4xx as `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED`; the step 2c refusal carries status 422. No edit needed there.
- Deviation 2 (full suites ran on `abd1ccea`, not the head): ANSWERED by CI on the head once Test Core concludes; in progress at 22:34Z, so the seat reads those eight conclusions before it queues.
- Deviation 3 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally): ANSWERED by CI; Build Core and the Lint · CI, release and engine gates concluded success on the head.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (CLI organization-ownership ceremony, "not filed"): ANSWERED, accepted as reported. Its save door writes no `object`; the SQL promotion goes to the boot path, which the card leaves unmoved.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (stale docblocks in `registry.ts` and `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`): ESCALATED to the seat as a follow-up card to file. After this PR those blocks say the batch writers and `registerApp` hear a refusal "only as a log line" and that `againstRegistry` is "not a batch publish, an install or a migration pass"; both are false at this head. Out of the claimed file surface, so not this PR's edit.
- `security_findings: none`: no security item found by this review either.
- BREAKING: the maintainer's word is owed before queueing (the dev states it; the PR body asks for it). ESCALATED to the seat; not answered by this record.
- Branch `claude/project-thread-610usd` in place of `claude/issue-N-slug`: declared on the claim as a platform exception; PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, attribution `os-bill`. File surface held: every changed path is inside the claim's surface (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/**`, `engine-registration.ts`, their tests, one `content/docs` sentence, the changeset).

### ④ Design judgment

F1 · must-fix · `packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts` step 2c. The unit it judges is smaller than the unit the tree registers.
- After the seal, an artifact's bodies register in one restore run, in order, and the residual's top-level objects after every body (`plugin.ts`: `ql.registry.restoringOnRefusal(() => { for (...) ql.registerApp(...); ...; registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects(...) })`). Step 2c asks at the end of each body, against whatever the registry holds at that moment.
- False refusal, first install: body A holds a line whose amount follows `PARENT.code`; the code field is supplied by a LATER member's `objectExtensions`. At A's step 2c the parent is registered without the field, the follow door refuses, and the whole artifact is put back. Before this PR it registered, and the finished artifact is a pair the door admits.
- False refusal, reload or upgrade: one reload adds the code field to the parent in a later member (or in the residual) and makes the child in an earlier body follow it. At the earlier body's step 2c the parent still registered is the OLD version, which lacks the field; refused, "the reload logs it and keeps the version that served". The same holds mirrored for a `record` roll-up in an earlier member over a child amount a later member makes follow. Both are valid artifacts that were answered registered before.
- Gap on the same unit: the residual's objects register through `registry.registerObject` directly after every body, and step 7's nested plugins register after step 2c, so neither is asked the follow door at all. A running install whose bad pair sits there is still registered and answered installed, which the card's scope addition (6782529809: "a package with a really bad follow pair reports the refusal in the install report") does not allow for the artifact route.
- This is the #29673 hazard the card's third acceptance bullet protects, and the one `registry.ts` names as the reason the follow door was opt-in ("a multi-registration unit after it ... has the same hazard"). The card's scope addition says "after step 2b for `registerApp`"; that is the right place for a single-body run and the wrong place for a joined run. Fix shape: ask once, when the OUTERMOST restore run has made its last registry write (the `registerApp` that opened the run, or the `manifest` service after the residual), over every object and extension the run registered, residual and nested plugins included; a `registerApp` that joined an open run defers. Pin: a two-member artifact whose later member's extension supplies the code field installs after the seal; a reload that moves both ends across members is admitted; a bad pair in the residual is refused.
- Not caught by the file's cases 8 and 10, which install one body.

F2 · should-fix · `protocol-history-and-publish.ts`. On a runtime that cannot roll back, the unit is judged only after every promotion is written, so each refused unit now goes through `undoLandedPromotions` (non-atomic, appends promote and undo history, can leave items LIVE). #32454 built Phase 0 so that a refusal it can see writes nothing; this refusal can be seen there (the same `judgeBatchObjectRegistrations` over the draft bodies the `judgeOnly` loop already reads). The answer is correct as it stands (`failed[]`, `stillLive` reported, pinned by case 5 on the memory driver), so not a must-fix; asking in Phase 0 when `!canRollBack` keeps #32454's property. The in-transaction placement before `recordPackageCommit` is right for a runtime that rolls back.

F3 · should-fix · `batch-object-registration.ts` `undoBatchRowWrite`, created-row arm. It reads the active row at undo time and deletes with THAT row's hash as `parentVersion`, so a concurrent writer's save to the same address between the batch's write and the settle is deleted without a conflict. Its precedent locks on the version the batch itself wrote (`undoLandedPromotions`: `parentVersion: item.version`). Carry the stamp `saveMetaItem` answered (or the hash `readActiveBatchRow` saw right after the write) and let a moved row surface as an undo failure, which the faces already report. The `restoreVersion` arm equals its precedent.

F4 · should-fix · `protocol-package-commits.ts` `duplicatePackage`. `copied.push` runs before the `readActiveBatchRow` read-back inside the same `try`; a store fault on that read lands the row in `copied[]` AND `failed[]`, stored, and outside the judged unit. Push after the read-back, or keep the read out of that `try`.

F5 · nit · `judgeBatchObjectRegistrations` `charge`. The refusal is charged to the first row whose object name equals the declaring `objectName`; when the unit holds both the object row and an `object_extension` row of the same object, an innocent one can be taken out first. `fieldName` on the refusal would pick the row that declares the field. The per-row loop still converges and the all-or-nothing faces are unaffected.

F6 · nit · migration restore fidelity. The undo is `restoreVersion(row.version)`, which needs a history snapshot at that version under the folded type; a legacy row without one cannot be restored. That failure is caught and reported in the row's `reason` ("could NOT be taken back ... correct it by hand"), so acceptance bullet 2 holds. The "taken back" text is also used when the store write succeeded and only the registry heal threw.

Held, tried and not broken:
- Pass loop: each pass strictly shrinks `left` or breaks; `settleBatchObjectRows` removes at least one row per round (a non-empty `lastRefusal` always yields a non-empty `refused`), so both terminate.
- A row admitted only because a later-refused sibling was in: the against-registry question is asked of every registered row after the passes, and the per-row faces judge the rest again after each undo; the all-or-nothing faces refuse on any refusal. A row admitted against a stale OLD sibling body (publish) is re-asked once the unit is whole.
- The judgement registers nothing: it always ends by throwing inside `restoringOnRefusal`, is synchronous, and is called from no open run (the publish transaction is the data engine's, not a registry run).
- An undo that itself fails: named in `failed[].error` / the row's `reason` and in a `console.warn`; the publish reports `stillLive`; the import reports its residue. A refused row left stored is always reported.
- Import: the registry's `code` / `status` ride the rollback error; the base is removed by the existing `deletePackage`.
- Tests: 10 cases on a real kernel and `SchemaRegistry`; three are the #29673 controls. No case pins an `object_extension` row through a batch writer, an undo that fails, or a multi-member artifact (F1).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c5a5de842f92b18480e050a776a679308c27a63`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/batch-object-registration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/metadata-registry-question-producers.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts (back to `main`, confirmed absent from the net diff), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`restoringOnRefusal`, `objectRegistrationRefusal`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`delete`, `lockAccepts`, the `checksum` column, `restoreVersion`), `promoteDraftForPublish` and `undoLandedPromotions` (PR #32454), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-unmanaged-import.ts: read at the head, not reviewed. Prose faces: .changeset/32369-batch-object-registration.md (semver, ②), content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx.

Round 2. Round 1 is comment 6808757636 on the PR (head `78122ffe`, FAIL on F1). This record judges the delta `78122ffe..7c5a5de8` (main's own commits set aside) and the net diff against `main` (10 files) where the delta touches it.

Inputs read: card #32369 body and its four comments (none added or edited since round 1); PR #32474 body as rewritten for this head, its file list and net diff; the round-1 record; the check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-12T00:24Z (54 runs), about two minutes after the push: 16 success, 17 skipped by path filter, 21 in progress, 0 failed. Success at that read: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, filter. NOT concluded at that read, so not part of this verdict: Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Live E2E UI, Test Core (1/8) to (8/8). The verdict below is the design verdict on the tree; the seat reads those conclusions before it queues, and a red one there overrides nothing here but stops the queue.

### ① Derived judgments

- `registerApp` after `kernel:bootstrapped`: no longer moved. RIGHT. `engine-registration.ts` is byte-for-byte `main` (not in the net diff), so a running install or reload registers what it registered before; the false refusal of round 1's F1 cannot occur and nothing valid is newly refused there.
- `external-import`, `duplicatePackage`, `importUnmanagedPackage`, `migrateStoredMetadata`: unchanged in what they accept and refuse since round 1; judged RIGHT there, and the delta moves only how an undo locks and how a failure is worded.
- `publishPackageDrafts`: same accept set as round 1 (RIGHT). On a runtime that cannot roll back, the same unit question is now also asked in Phase 0 over the draft bodies, so a refused unit promotes nothing. It refuses nothing Phase 1 would not: one judge (`judgeBatchObjectRegistrations`), the same rows, the same registry.
- `promoteDraftForPublish`'s declared answer gains optional `judged: { body, packageId }`, present only on a `judgeOnly` call that read a draft. Additive: no caller reads it but `publishPackageDrafts`' Phase 0; a write call's answer is unchanged. RIGHT.
- Public surface otherwise as in round 1: `AGAINST_REGISTRY_SAVE_FACES` gains `external-import`; one internal module, now also exporting `BatchRowHealError` and `undoOutcomeForLog` for its two faces. No `packages/spec` path.
- Declared unmoved, and unmoved in the tree: the boot, the stored-row hydration, a code package installed or reloaded on a running server, a draft save.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, alone. RIGHT: it is the only package whose shipped source the net diff moves (`packages/objectql` and `packages/runtime` change a test file each), and kind `narrowed` takes at least `minor`.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; the title carries `!`; the BREAKING banner and FROM/TO list are in both and no longer name `registerApp`; the ADR-0087 marker is unchanged in kind and its sentence no longer claims a package registered after the boot. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- The changeset's "what does not change" now names `registerApp`, and its publish bullet states the Phase 0 route. Both match the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 flags stand as answered there (deviation 1 is now moot: no install path is edited; deviation 3 is closed by the dev's own run of `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, exit 0, and by CI once Build Core concludes).
- ESCALATED to the seat, owed before queueing: the removal of step 2c is a seat ruling that exists only in the PR body. Card #32369's scope addition (6782529809) puts post-seal `registerApp` in this card and adds two acceptance bullets for it; the PR says `Fixes #32369`, so a merge closes the card with that half unbuilt. The ruling and the follow-up card's number belong on #32369 (and the scope addition marked moved) before the merge; the PR body says "the seat files that" and names no number.
- ESCALATED to the seat: the os-dev-report on the card (6808545455) is round 1's. It still lists `engine-registration.ts` as changed and describes step 2c; it has no entry for `protocol.ts`. `protocol.ts` is inside the claim's file surface (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/**`), and the claim asked for minimal edits there because of #30020: the touch is one optional field on a declared answer, which is minimal. A refreshed report is the dev's to post.
- ESCALATED, unchanged: the maintainer's word on the BREAKING narrowing; the follow-up for the stale docblocks in `registry.ts` and `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts` (the PR body folds it into the same follow-up card).
- `open_questions`: still empty. No security item found.

### ④ Design judgment

Round-1 findings:
- F1 (must-fix): CLOSED by removal. Consistency of the removal checked: no `engine-registration.ts` hunk remains; the two `registerApp` test cases are gone; `registry-question.ts`'s header and producers table never named `registerApp` and need no edit; `currency.mdx` now says objects registered "by a code package installed or reloaded on a running server are not judged this way" and says "unmanaged install" for the face that is; the changeset and the PR body agree. Nothing left half-said in the diff. The running-install judgement is not delivered by this PR (③).
- F2 (should-fix): CLOSED. Phase 0 collects each `judgeOnly` answer's `judged` body for object types and judges them as one unit before any promotion; the causal draft is tagged from an index-aligned list. Pinned: no history event, both drafts still pending, `BATCH_ABORTED` "nothing was promoted". Double refusal: none, the Phase 0 throw precedes Phase 1 and the `catch` runs once. Disagreement: Phase 0 judges the draft body, Phase 1 the promoted body, against the same registry; where they differ (a derived active body, or a registry that moved between the phases) Phase 1 refuses and `undoLandedPromotions` undoes, which is #32454's stated route for "a refusal only the earlier promotions provoke". A sealed managed object never reaches the unit judge: its `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` refusal is thrown before `judged` is returned. On a runtime that rolls back, Phase 0 does not run and the in-transaction question is the only one, as in round 1.
- F3 (should-fix): CLOSED. The created-row arm deletes under `writtenHash`, the row's `checksum` read right after the batch's write, which is the stored stamp `SysMetadataRepository.delete` locks on (`lockAccepts`); an unknown stamp throws instead of deleting. A row moved since surfaces as a conflict and is reported as an undo failure. Pinned by a write between the copy and its undo. The migration never takes this arm.
